title: Allele-specific and multiplex PCR based tools for cost-effective and comprehensive genetic testing in Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia
author: Ravichandran, Varghese, et al.
materials:
A multiplex PCR program was designed to comprehensively screen for CYP21A2, CYP11B1, CYP17A1 and POR genes in CAH along with the CYP19A1 gene that causes aromatase deficiency mimicking CAH. The coding and splice site regions of four genes - CYP11B1, CYP17A1, POR and CYP19A1 were amplified in 28 amplicons in 6 groups. Primers for the CYP11B1 gene were adapted from white et al.
[6]. The primers were pooled into six groups based on the amplicon sizes (Table 3 and 4). The multiplex PCR was carried out using QIAGEN® Multiplex PCR kit. The PCR reaction mix and the conditions are described in table 5 and 6 respectively. The concentration of primers used was 10 pmol/µl. The PCR products were visualized on 2% agarose gel electrophoresis (Fig. 5.). Multiplex PCR products were pooled along with the long range PCR product of CYP21A2 gene and sequencing with Ion Torrent PGM™ was performed following methods from published protocols [7]. Multiplex PCR coupled NGS sequencing achieved a uniform coverage across five genes with an average base coverage depth of 700X and with >99% of the target having 20X coverage (Table 7 and steps.title: Extract genomic DNA from blood
steps.instruction: Collect 2 ml of EDTA‑anticoagulated whole blood and isolate genomic DNA using the Gentra Puregene kit (QIAGEN, Hilden, Germany) according to the manufacturer’s instructions; quantify the eluate with a NanoDrop™ spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Amplify CYP21A2 and CYP21A1P by long-range PCR
steps.instruction: Set up two long‑range PCRs (≈6.2 kb for CYP21A2 and ≈6.1 kb for CYP21A1P) using the TaKaRa LA PCR™ Kit (ver. 2.1) and the primer pairs CYP779f/Tena36F (functional gene) and CYP779f/XA‑36F (pseudogene) as described in Lee et al.; run the reactions under the published cycling conditions.

steps.title: Validate PCR products with TaqI restriction digestion
steps.instruction: Digest each long‑range PCR product with TaqI restriction enzyme following the protocol of reference [1]; analyse the digested fragments on a 1 % agarose gel to confirm the expected band sizes (functional gene: 3.7 kb + 2.4 kb; pseudogene: 3.2 kb + 2.3 kb).

steps.title: Purify long-range PCR product with AMPure XP beads
steps.instruction: Clean‑up the long‑range PCR amplicon using Agencourt AMPure XP magnetic beads (Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, USA) according to the manufacturer’s protocol; elute the purified DNA for use as template in ASPCR.

steps.title: Set up allele-specific PCR (ASPCR) reaction
steps.instruction: Prepare a 15 µl ASPCR mix with the following components: 7.5 µl Emerald Amp® Max PCR master mix (Takara Bio), 1 µl wild‑type forward primer (10 pmol µl⁻¹), 1 µl mutant forward primer (10 pmol µl⁻¹), 1 µl common reverse primer (10 pmol µl⁻¹), 1 µl internal forward primer (10 pmol µl⁻¹), 1 µl internal reverse primer (10 pmol µl⁻¹), 1 µl purified long‑range PCR product (adjusted to 5–8 ng µl⁻¹), and 2.5 µl sterile water.

steps.title: Run ASPCR thermal cycling program
steps.instruction: Place the ASPCR tubes in a thermal cycler and run: initial denaturation 95 °C for 5 min; 20 cycles of 98 °C for 10 s, annealing at 68 °C (70 °C for the I2G assay) for 30 s, extension at 72 °C for 1 min; final extension at 72 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Analyze ASPCR products on agarose gel
steps.instruction: Load the ASPCR reactions onto a 2 % agarose gel alongside a positive control (PC), negative control (NC), and no‑template control (NTC); run electrophoresis and visualise bands (internal control ≈180 bp, mutant‑specific bands of expected size).

steps.title: Perform MLPA for large deletions confirmation
steps.instruction: For samples suspected of a 30 kbp deletion or gene conversion, carry out MLPA using the SALSA MLPA CAH Probemix P050 C1 (MRC‑Holland) according to the kit protocol; analyse probe copy numbers to confirm loss of CYP21A2 probes.

steps.title: Prepare multiplex PCR for NGS panel
steps.instruction: Combine the primer pools for CYP21A2, CYP11B1, CYP17A1, POR and CYP19A1 as described in Tables 3–4 (six groups). For each 15 µl reaction add: 7.5 µl 2× QIAGEN Multiplex PCR Master Mix, 1.5 µl Q‑solution, 1 µl genomic DNA (template), 3 µl pooled primers (10 pmol µl⁻¹ per primer), and 2 µl sterile water.

steps.title: Run multiplex PCR thermal cycling program
steps.instruction: Program the thermal cycler: initial denaturation 95 °C for 10 min; 98 °C for 5 min; 25 cycles of 98 °C for 30 s, annealing at 60 °C for 90 s, extension at 72 °C for 90 s; final extension at 72 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: Visualize multiplex PCR products on agarose gel
steps.instruction: Separate the multiplex PCR amplicons on a 2 % agarose gel; confirm the presence of all expected band sizes for the six primer groups.

steps.title: Pool PCR products and sequence on Ion Torrent
steps.instruction: Pool the six multiplex PCR products together with the purified long‑range CYP21A2 amplicon; prepare an Ion Torrent PGM library following the published protocol [7]; sequence on the Ion Torrent PGM and analyse coverage (target ≥20×, average depth ≈700×).
